summary: Absecon Light, Atlantic City, New Jersey: 1857 first-order Fresnel tower, discontinued 1933; state-owned and open, with the tower climbable.

structures.type: conical brick and iron tower attached to keepers' dwelling
structures.note: 171 ft per nomination and LighthouseFriends; 159 ft base to lantern per USLHS

access.note: Grounds, keeper's dwelling and tower are open (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (owner); Inlet Public/Private Association listed as manager by USLHS

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination gives 1856 for the erection and the Society gives 1857 as the year the tower was established; LighthouseFriends dates the start of work to June 1855 and the first light to 15 January 1857. Both 1856 and 1857 are in the story, with the disagreement stated.
171 ft (nomination, LighthouseFriends) against 159 ft base to lantern (USLHS). The story gives 171 ft and states the Society's figure.

notes_for_editor: (1) Roster: all 31 USLHS lines are printed as the archive prints them and carry its person slugs; they are the NARA-register inventory, not verified line by line against NARA. (2) The USLHS place record says Active Aid to Navigation: Yes and Year Discontinued 1933-1997; the nomination and LighthouseFriends say the light was decommissioned or deactivated in 1933. The story states both; the record's status field (active) needs a human decision. (3) The earthquake log date (30 August 1886, 9:52 p.m.) comes from LighthouseFriends, which quotes the logbook; the logbook image and a dated newspaper were not checked (Chronicling America searches for 1886 returned nothing for Absecon). (4) OCR of the 1970 nomination is poor. The name of the officer who directed construction is unreadable in the scan, so the story does not name him from the nomination; LighthouseFriends names Lt. George Meade among the supervising officers. (5) Museum opening: the nomination (1970) describes a small museum; LighthouseFriends dates the Atlantic City Coastal Museum's opening to 1979. Not resolved. (6) Owner and manager: the record's agency field names the Inlet Public/Private Association as manager; LighthouseFriends and the nomination name the New Jersey DEP as owner. (7) Opening hours come from LighthouseFriends and may be out of date. (8) The 1917 Commissioner's report table (corpus scan p.266) lists J. H. Woods, keeper, against Absecon Light Station; he is not on the USLHS roster for Absecon. The table's column layout was not read in full, so he is not used. (9) Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it, with one short quotation of a sentence in the log entry. (10) The Lighthouse Board's 1857 to 1858 report that LighthouseFriends quotes is not in the local corpus; the quotation is cited to LighthouseFriends. (11) Kate W. Wolf is listed on the roster as a first assistant; the sources do not say whether she was related to Abraham G. Wolf. (12) Log date: LighthouseFriends gives 30 August 1886 at 9:52 p.m. The USGS Publications Warehouse (Pratt et al. 2022, cited as note 11 in the story) dates the Charleston earthquake to 31 August 1886; the USGS event page gives 02:51 UTC on 1 September 1886, which is about 9:51 p.m. Eastern time on 31 August. The logged time matches the quake's time within a minute, so the log date may be a day out. The story states the disagreement and does not link the two events. Check the logbook image before publication. (13) The 1912 and 1925 Bulletin dates were checked in the PDF text: the 1925 change is listed under the heading for July 1925, so the story says July 1925. (14) The 1893 Board report prints the Floriday wreck heading with OCR 'Life-8aving'; the story uses the name as the OCR gives it. Ship name not checked against a newspaper.
